meta.description: Character LoRA on base SDXL for a 16GB laptop GPU. Recipe values (rank 32/alpha 32 + conv 16/16, adamw8bit, LR 1e-4, 1024 training resolution) are UNCHANGED from sdxl_char_lora. The point of this variant is batch discipline: this preset keeps batch 1 and reaches an effective batch of 2 via gradient_accumulation 2, which costs wall-clock instead of VRAM. Effective batch 2, not 4: the step suggestion divides by effective batch, and at 4 that quotient drops under the arch's step floor on any small/medium dataset, gets clamped back up, and silently inflates real per-image exposure 2-3x past target - the advisor then recommends a step count its own exposure gauge would flag as fry-risk. The in-app advisor now also recommends batch 2 for SDXL, so the two agree; note it is still VRAM-unaware, so on this machine reach effective batch through accumulation as configured here rather than raising batch size. Other deltas vs sdxl_char_lora: low_vram true (parks idle components on CPU - cheap with a large system-RAM pool), cache_latents true alongside cache_latents_to_disk so latents are served from RAM rather than re-read and deep-copied from disk every step (native Windows runs the dataloader at num_workers 0, so disk reads are serialized with GPU compute), and ui_db_poll_seconds 2 to throttle the UI's per-step sqlite polling (cost: up to 2s of latency on the stop/save-now buttons). SDXL is left unquantized, matching the family default on both sides of the LDS/ATK preset alignment - a 2.6B unet in bf16 has room to spare here, so quantization is held in reserve as an OOM lever rather than spent up front. Preview sampling stays at 1024 (SDXL's native resolution, and cheap relative to the flux-family models). NOT measured on 16GB hardware. Point model.name_or_path at any SDXL-family checkpoint (RealVis, Juggernaut, etc.) to train on it instead. If you swap the optimizer to an Automagic variant, this batch-1-plus-accumulation pattern will not work as-is - Automagic fuses its step into the backward pass by default, so gradient_accumulation must go back to 1 and the effective batch reached by raising batch size instead. Speed (2026-08-29): latents are served from RAM after the first pass (cache_latents + cache_latents_to_disk — disk-only caching re-read every latent every step), loss_sync_every 4, ui_db_poll_seconds 2. Training math unchanged. STEP TABLE (meta.step_table, 2026-10-12, evidence-based Illustrious/NoobAI table, machine-independent - the same table ships on every IllustriousXL and SDXL preset, laptop or desktop, character or style): 20 images ~1600, 30 images ~2000, 40 images ~2500, 50 images ~3000, exact-count interpolation between rows, capped at 3000 steps. OPTIMIZED DATASET COUNT ~50 images: that is where the cap is reached; past it the panel keeps 3000 and the exposure gauge says the dataset is past the optimal size for this model and suggests curating down, instead of calling it undertrained. Sources: character LoRAs converge at a roughly fixed ~1500-2000 total steps (Illustrious kohya guide, civitai.com/models/850658: ~1500 steps per character; DCAI Illustrious and NoobAI character guides: 1600 steps; civitai.com/articles/21604 NoobAI: 1900-2000; civitai.com/articles/9148: 2500-3000 at lower LR), style LoRAs want ~3000 steps on ~50 images (civitai.com/articles/25645), and 20-30 images 2000-3000 (r/StableDiffusion primer). Values are steps at effective batch 1; the Step Suggestion panel divides by your effective batch (batch_size x gradient_accumulation), which is the only thing that differs between machines. Below the first row the first row's steps apply.
